description:
Every command arm that accepts the machine-readable output flag reports its failures in the structured error envelope, so a machine consumer never has to parse a plain-text diagnostic line.

## Background

The machine-readable contract covers success output but not failure. An arm renders the structured envelope on failure only when it classifies the error itself and hands it to the shared error handler at `crates/jit/src/output_macros.rs:70`; an arm that propagates its error with a bare `?` reaches the top-level printer instead, which writes a plain-text `Error: <message>` line. Both forms carry the same exit code, so a consumer that only checks status sees no difference — but the plain-text form carries no error code, no structured detail, and nothing a JSON parser can read.

Measured on the current tree: 18 call sites route failures through the shared handler, against roughly 63 command arms that accept the flag. Confirmed by invocation against a missing or invalid argument — `issue show`, `gate status`, `item show`, and `dep add` emit the envelope; `doc list`, `doc show`, and `graph deps` emit a plain-text line. So the defect is neither universal nor confined to one namespace, and which arms are affected is not derivable from the command surface itself.

The `doc` namespace is where it surfaced: eight arms there (`add`, `list`, `remove`, `show`, `history`, `diff`, `assets list`, `check-links`) propagate with a bare `?`, and `doc dir` was repaired in place, establishing the pattern — classify the failure by downcast, then hand the envelope to the shared handler.

This surface is what the MCP bridge is generated from, so an agent consumer reaching a failing arm receives output it cannot decode into a failure reason.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A census derived from the command definitions, rather than from sampling, records for every arm accepting the machine-readable output flag whether its failure path renders the structured envelope.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every arm accepting the flag renders its failures as the structured error envelope carrying a classified error code, with no arm reaching the top-level plain-text printer.
- [hard] REQ-03: A failing invocation under the flag emits no plain-text diagnostic on the stream that carries the envelope.
- [hard] REQ-04: A converted arm's process exit code equals the code its envelope reports, and failures of the same class exit identically across arms.
- [hard] REQ-05: Regression coverage drives a failing invocation of every converted arm and asserts envelope structure and error classification rather than a copied message string.
- [hard] REQ-06: A repository check fails when an arm accepting the flag can reach the top-level plain-text printer on failure, so a newly added arm cannot ship without the envelope.
- [hard] REQ-07: Adopter documentation states the machine-readable failure contract — envelope shape, error code, exit code — once, in a single canonical home.

## Non-goals

- Changing the human-readable failure output of any command.
- Restructuring the success-side envelope or its collection wrapper.
- Revising the error-code vocabulary or exit-code assignment for arms that already render the envelope.
- Adding the flag to command arms that do not accept it today.

## Notes

- Scope is the whole command surface rather than the `doc` namespace alone, and delivery is in milestone v1.0: the plain-text failure form is a release-visible contract defect on the surface generated agent tooling consumes, and the repair pattern is already established in the tree.
- REQ-07 is subject to `@/charter/D-13`: one canonical home per adopter-facing fact.
- REQ-06 is what separates this from a sweep. The census in REQ-01 goes stale the moment a new arm is added, so the guard is the durable half of the work.
title: Structured failure reporting across the machine-readable CLI surface
